name: The New York World's cross-word puzzle, in its Sunday FUN supplement
numbering: printed in the grid's shaded center cross, "No. n" (No. 7 on 1914-02-01, No. 8 on 1914-02-08); gone by 1917
status: the series this repo tracks: one row per Sunday in status.tsv; World dates inferred from the number (see README)
source: Minneapolis Journal reprints, Newspapers.com, Alex DeJarnatt 2026-10-27; first-runs.md in the catalog

name: The World's FUN puzzle reprinted in The Minneapolis Journal
to: unknown; by 1920-03 running "Jerry King's Cross-Word Puzzle" instead
numbering: the World's grid number; the Journal's own heading "No. 5" on 1914-02-01 was wrong and dropped
answers: the next Sunday, often on the same page as the next puzzle
status: main source of copies: to clip, one per Sunday

name: The World's FUN puzzle reprinted in The Pittsburgh Press
status: fallback source when the Journal stops carrying FUN; autumn 1918 gap (Alex browsed the issues): no crossword on 09-22, 09-29, 10-06, 10-13 or 11-24; after the 09-15 key (answers 09-08) come the one-off Liberty Loan (10-20) and Stars & Stripes (10-27) word-crosses, a 11-03 page with only the 10-27 key, and FUN again on 11-10

name: Fun's Cross-Word Puzzle in the Tacoma Daily Ledger
answers: weeks behind the World: the Globe's 1917-02-25 puzzle ran 1917-03-11
status: fallback source; copies run about two weeks late

name: The World's FUN puzzle reprinted in The Boston Globe, without credit
to: unknown (by 1923 the Globe had its own)
answers: printings to match to World puzzles by clues, not a source to clip here

name: Jerry King's Cross-Word Puzzle, later Crossword Puzzle Corner, in The Pittsburgh Press
status: NOT the World's series and not matched to it: a catalog lead for the Pittsburgh Press entry, outside this repo's scope. The World's FUN run in the Press ends after 1919-12-14 (a key-only page); Alex reports a break until this series. The Press printed it as Jerry King's Cross-Word Puzzle (copyright 1920 W. A. Walker, about 21x21, first clue 1-9 Having unusually early intelligence); around 1924 (approximate, Alex's recollection) it becomes Crossword Puzzle Corner, still credited to Jerry King. Clues not indexed.
